newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor tax situation in order - Finmin.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor tax situation in order - Finmin.

text.p: The tax position of cement group Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal is in order and the company has no outstanding debts to the authorities, the Finance Ministry said, clarifying a news report.
The ministry said in a statement that there had been a problem with a tax return in the early 1990s but this issue had been completely resolved.
It denied that it had agreed to absorb an outstanding tax liability of six billion escudos ($39 million) as suggested in news reports on Tuesday.
"It is totally false that the Treasury has taken on a tax debt of six billion escudos," it said.
It said the tax position of the company, which is being privatised, had been recently put in order although this had nothing to do with the sale of a further state stake.

The difficulty had stemmed from the fact that the tax authorities had not accepted provisions made in 1991 against doubtful debt. The authorities said that it should have been made in the following two years.
"As a result, Cimpor owed for 1991 but was owed a similar amount for 1992 and 1993," the ministry said.
